findings.title: MSNightmare/SignDrop GitHub repository (original researcher disclosure)
findings.summary_md: The researcher publishing as MSNightmare created this repository on November 10, 2026 with the description 'Windows Common Log FileSystem Authentication 0day Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability.' The write-up explains the flaw in clfs.sys: when a standard user creates a log and a privileged process is later coerced to open it, CLFS creates the missing .cnpf authentication (HMAC) file under the privileged context, and the file inherits the original DACL, yielding a SYSTEM shell. The PoC coerces Windows Defender to open the container via ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, ships C++ source with a Visual Studio project, and was tested on Windows 11 26H2, 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental. It notes the CLFS authentication mitigation rolled out on or after October 28, 2025, and gives a registry check at HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode where values 0 or 1 are vulnerable and 2 or 3 are not.

findings.title: SignDrop Windows CLFS Zero-Day Gives SYSTEM Access
findings.summary_md: Cyber Kendra reported on November 11, 2026 that the researcher (handles MSNightmare, Chaotic Eclipse, Nightmare-Eclipse) had posted a working SignDrop proof-of-concept on GitHub the previous day with no coordinated disclosure. The article confirms the flaw has no CVE ID and no CVSS score and that Microsoft had published neither advisory nor fix as of that date. It details the mechanism: the CLFS authentication mitigation stores an HMAC in a .cnpf file beside each log, and SignDrop coerces the Defender antimalware engine into opening a user-prepared log so the signature file is written as SYSTEM and inherits the original permissions. It notes the researcher's claim that the technique can disable other antivirus and EDR products, that the mitigation reached Windows 11 25H2 and Windows Server 2025 in updates on or after October 28, 2025, that both learning and enforcement modes are affected, and that the bug requires an attacker to already run code locally as a standard user.
